definitions.explanation: March 14th, one month after Valentine's Day, when men give return gifts to women who gave them chocolate

notes:
A holiday unique to Japan (and some other East Asian countries). Created by the confectionery industry in the late 1970s as a counterpart to Valentine's Day. On March 14th, men who received chocolate on Valentine's Day are expected to give return gifts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ホワイトデー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{返|かえ}し→お返し：08354_okaeshi⟧: White Day return gift
- ホワイトデー⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{贈|おく}る→贈る：09862_okuru⟧: to give on White Day
- {三倍返|さんばいがえ}し: returning three times the value
- ホワイトデー⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦プレゼント→プレゼント：01791_purezento⟧: White Day present

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional return gifts include cookies, candy, marshmallows, or accessories. There is an unwritten expectation that the return gift should be of equal or greater value than the chocolate received. In workplace contexts, men often give group gifts in return for ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧チョコ received. The concept of ⟦{倍返|ばいがえ}し→倍返し：18081_baigaeshi⟧ (returning double or triple the value) adds social pressure to the occasion.
